TENSION: {A} and {B} have been at war for a generation over {W}; {C} sells to both sides.
{A} holds the throne of one castle and {B} wants it; {C} is neutral until someone pays.

STORYLINE: An artifact in three pieces, one in each faction's keeping. Assembled, it does something the dungeon won't describe.
A mad mage has turned himself into an elemental and is the real power behind one castle.
A feral god's egg is buried under the neutral quadrant. Every faction knows. None of them will say it.
The dome is failing early. The factions blame each other. The clock on the wall is wrong.
One faction's ruler is a former crawler from a past season. They remember the rules better than you do.
The castles' thrones are linked: sit on one and the other three rulers feel it.
THRONE_NOTE: The throne is real. Sitting on it counts. Standing next to it does not.
The throne room is above the stairwell, not beside it. Take the room, then find the trapdoor.
The throne is occupied by something that is not the boss. Killing it still counts.
Throne room doors seal when the boss drops below half. Nobody in, nobody out.
Two thrones. One is a mimic. The dungeon finds this very funny.
The throne room is flooded to the waist. The stairwell is dry. Nobody knows how.
APPROACH: Front gate is a killing field; the service entrance is real but guarded by the faction that built it.
The garrison rotates every twelve hours; the changeover is the window.
A civilian population lives inside. Collateral is on the crawlers.
The castle's defenses are automated and stupid. Its ruler is not.
There is a traitor inside who will open a door, once, for a price.
Nothing inside is hostile until the throne room. Then all of it is.
OBSTACLE: A hangar/dock full of the castle's vehicles, crewed and fueled.
A great hall of feasting guests who are also the garrison.
A puzzle door keyed to the faction's language.
A vault of cages; what's inside can be freed or used.
A chapel where the faction's god actually answers.
A bridge that only bears the weight of one crawler at a time.
An armory. Everything in it is trapped, and everything in it is good.
